description: REQ-T3 says sanitize 'name' through a '[a-z0-9_-]' filter dropping other chars. EDGE-E2 covers ONLY empty input ('name field is empty'). But common menu.json names contain Japanese (e.g. 'スキャン-coconala', from the gig menu domain) or uppercase ASCII. Post-sanitization, an all-non-matching name (e.g. 'スキャンリクエスト') becomes the empty string, which then collides with the EDGE-E2 'unnamed-<ts>' fallback semantically but NOT structurally — REQ-T3 says 'drop other chars' producing '', not invoke E2 fallback. Spec must define: (a) does the sanitizer also lowercase ASCII (current regex implies yes by exclusion but unstated), and (b) what is the filename when sanitized output is empty? If 'unnamed-<ts>', state it; if empty-string is acceptable producing '<ts>-.json', state that. Without this an implementation choice is forced on the builder and adversary cannot test deterministically.

evidence.snippet: REQ-T3: THE filename <sanitized_name> SHALL be the menu item's `name` field passed through a `[a-z0-9_-]` sanitizer (= drop other chars).

secondaryEvidence.snippet: EDGE-E2 | menu item name is empty | enqueue with unnamed-<ts> filename
